title: Premier Deductible Reimbursement: Computation of the Deductible Covered
content:
**GAP Waiver Addenda, GAP Waiver Premier 150 claims.** This section sets how the Premier deductible reimbursement is figured.

**1. The claim.** The claim is the latest claim reported on the addendum, meaning the claim with the latest reporting date. Where two claims were reported on that date, the one recorded first on the addendum counts. The deductible withheld is the primary deductible that this claim shows the primary insurer deducted.

**2. The declarations read.** The declarations are those on the latest proof of insurance that the contract's insurance tracking record shows as accepted. The latest accepted proof is the accepted proof with the latest review date. Where two were reviewed on that date, the one recorded first counts.

**3. The declared deductible.** The declared deductible taken from those declarations is the lower of their comprehensive deductible and their collision deductible.

**4. The reimbursement maximum.** The reimbursement maximum is 250.00.

**5. The reimbursement.** The Premier deductible reimbursement is the deductible the primary insurer actually deducted, as the claim's deductible withheld shows it, subject to these limits:

- it is up to the reimbursement maximum;
- it is never more than the declared deductible when that is above 0.00;
- it is rounded half-up to the cent.

With no declarations read, it is the deductible withheld up to the reimbursement maximum. A deductible the insurer did not withhold is never reimbursed, and the figure is never below 0.00.

### Judgement table

| Deductible withheld | Declarations read | Declared deductible | Premier deductible reimbursement |
|---|---|---|---|
| above 0.00 | yes | above 0.00 | the lowest of the withheld deductible, the declared deductible and the reimbursement maximum |
| above 0.00 | yes | 0.00 | the withheld deductible up to the reimbursement maximum |
| above 0.00 | none | none | the withheld deductible up to the reimbursement maximum |
| 0.00 | any | any | 0.00 |

### Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Suppose the claim shows a deductible withheld of 615.00. The latest accepted proof declares a collision deductible of 410.00 and a comprehensive deductible of 185.00, so the declared deductible is the lower of the two, 185.00. That is below the 250.00 maximum, so the reimbursement is 185.00. Had those declarations shown 0.00 deductibles, the reimbursement would be the withheld 615.00 up to the 250.00 maximum, which is 250.00.
